description: Reading a table tagged against a different registry (AMB-059).

local.name: oil
local.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1
name = "oil"
version = "1.4"
[unit.m]
dimension = "length"
factor = [1, 1]
[unit.bbl]
dimension = "length"
factor = [9938205933, 62500000000]
display = { long = "oil barrel" }

foreign.name: water
foreign.toml:
[registry]
schema_version = 1
name = "water"
version = "2.1"
[unit.m]
dimension = "length"
factor = [1, 1]
[unit.bbl]
dimension = "length"
factor = [29810117799, 250000000000]
display = { long = "water barrel" }

cases.rationale: The case AMB-059 was opened for. Both tables tag `bbl`; canonical form is registry-relative so the strings match and the dimensions match, while the quantities differ by 33%. Before the boundary check this joined silently. The diagnostic must carry the magnitude — "factors differ" is not actionable.

cases.rationale: A version bump that adds `acre_ft` without touching anything in use. This is why the rule compares symbols rather than pins: a pin comparison would reject every version bump, and version bumps are the common case.

foreign.name: b
foreign.toml:

schema_version = 1
name = "b"
version = "1"
[unit.degC]
dimension = "temperature"

cases.rationale: Affine units fail differently: identical factor, moved zero. Comparing scale alone would pass this, and the column would be wrong by the offset at every value.

cases.rationale: The cost of §5.6's `pin` embedding mode, made explicit. "Could not check" is a different claim from "checked and fine", and collapsing them is exactly the silence this entry is about. The diagnostic must name the remedy: obtain the registry, or republish with it embedded.
